title: Mass ratio calculation
description: Essential: The final answer for part (1) must be the correct mass ratio, 19/36 or its decimal equivalent.

title: Initial pressure of B
description: Important: The student must correctly calculate the initial pressure of gas B as 90 cmHg by adding the mercury column pressure to gas A's pressure.

title: Boyle's law for masses
description: Important: The student must apply Boyle's law to relate the initial pressures and volumes of A and B to find the ratio of their masses.

title: Final piston displacement
description: Essential: The final answer for part (2) must be the correct displacement, approximately 3.35 cm.

title: Post-compression pressures
description: Important: The student must correctly find the new pressures for gases A and B after the piston is moved, using the given final pressure for B.

title: Boyle's law for compression
description: Important: The student must apply Boyle's law separately to gases A and B to find their new lengths after the piston is moved.

title: Displacement from geometry
description: Important: The student must correctly combine the changes in lengths of columns A and B to find the total piston displacement.

title: Pressure sign error
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the student incorrectly sets the pressure relationship between A and B, e.g., subtracting the mercury column when they should add it.

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional: The student maintains consistent use of cmHg for pressure and cm for length throughout the calculation.
